`cargo build` is ROUTED through `cargo cooldown`, the backend at /root/.cargo/bin/cargo-cooldown answers --version, and the wrapper pins the window in the environment - OBSERVED handing it COOLDOWN_MINUTES=2880 (48h) when the caller had exported 0, so no cooldown.toml anywhere can widen it. CAPPED AT WEAK ON PURPOSE: these are observations of OUR wrapper; cargo-cooldown never reported the window back and nothing here watched it refuse a crate - the same honest cap as the pnpm age-gate row

the wrapper pins incompatible-publish-age='deny' in the environment - OBSERVED handed to cargo-cooldown over a caller's 'allow' - which outranks every cooldown.toml, a repo's own included. deny is documented (harden.sh, the role's cooldown.toml) as failing the command and restoring the original Cargo.lock; that semantic is quoted, not measured here

`cargo build` is routed through the age gate but these lockfile WRITERS are not: add generate-lockfile vendor remove. cooldown.toml sets lockfile-baseline='floor', so every later gated build ACCEPTS whatever they pinned - one `cargo add` switches the gate off for every build after it. The wrapper prints a 'writes Cargo.lock and is NOT age-gated' warning for each of them, but a warning is not a gate. No configuration closes this: cargo-cooldown has no subcommand for these writers. See https://github.com/echennells/supply-chain-hardening/blob/main/docs/design-principles.md#gated-the-entry-points-missed-the-state-writers
the wrapper routes cargo through sfw but sfw is not on PATH - crate downloads are unfiltered
